svg.title: Label-preserving intensity transforms for spine segmentation
svg.desc: Eight small line plots of the same toy intensity profile along the spine, alternating vertebral bodies with bright cortical endplates and darker intervertebral discs, each under one augmentation: the original CT-like profile, intensity inversion, histogram equalisation, unsharp masking, Scharr edge magnitude, a random convolution, RedistributeSeg and a smooth bias field. Under every plot a coloured strip marks the vertebrae in blue and the discs in orange, and it is identical in all eight panels, because the transforms change only intensities, never the labels. Inversion makes discs brighter than bone, the edge map peaks at every boundary, and RedistributeSeg shifts each labelled region by a different amount.
svg.text: x + a_r p̂_r(x) inside region r
The anatomy y is fixed; each augmentation redraws the intensity map x = g(y)
Toy intensity profile along the spine, one line per transform T(x); the coloured strip under each is the unchanged label
Inversion turns bright bone dark (CT toward T2-like); the CDF, edge and convolution maps discard absolute intensity and keep
structure. RedistributeSeg reads the mask, so it exists only at training time. Nothing formal ties this family to the real
CT/MRI intensity mappings: covering unseen contrasts is an empirical bet.
